note: Both sets extract the same six core facts (design-point TSR 9.0 and pitch 0°, optimal TSR 8.5 and pitch −1.0°, up to 4° positive pitch at low wind speed, force peak near 90 m) with values, units and quotes that match the page. Set B adds 'maximum CP' as the condition for the optimal TSR/pitch pair, which is a reasonable reading of the text ('optimal' referenced to the CP curve), and labels the 90 m claim as blade forces rather than blade, both defensible. Neither set misreads or invents anything, and both omit the same secondary facts, so the sets are effectively equivalent in correctness and coverage.
remarks: Both sets omit several engineering facts on the page: Region 3 torque saturation at rated torque with pitch-to-feather to hold rated rotor speed, the negligible Region 2.5 with little influence from set point smoothing/peak shaving, the sharp linear force drop over the outboard 5% of the blade caused by the Prandtl tip loss model, and the tip unloading trade-off (tower-strike prevention vs. lost power). Set B's 'maximum CP' condition for the optimal point is mildly interpretive but consistent with the text's reference to the CP curve.
